 Judgment

The petitioner has filed the present claim petition against the respondents under section 166 of MV Act seeking compensation towards the accidental injuries from date of accident till the date of payment together with cost and interest.

2. The factual matrix of the petition in the nutshell is as follows:
This petition is represented by next friend of the petitioner i.e., his son by name S.D.Ashwin.
On 22.01.2022 at about 06.30 p.m., the petitioner was crossing the road on Vajarahalli, 100 feet road, near Kalikamba Nandini booth.
At that time one Tata Ace bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3437 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact of a accident the petitioner fell down and has sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Aster RV Hospital Bengaluru wherein first aid treatment and then admitted as an inpatient from 21.01.2022 to 16.02.2022.

The x-ray report revealed that he had sustained severe head injury, diffuse axonal injury, sub archnoid hemorrhage and other injuries and under went tracheostomy was done on 29.01.2022 with an advice continuing follow up treatment with complete bed rest and he taking physiotherapy treatment every day by paying Rs.1,000/- per day.
4.

The petitioner further pleaded that he has incurred Rs.20,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
conveyance, medical treatment, attendant, nursing care and other incidental expenses.
He is in need of future medical treatment and other incidental expenses.
5. Petitioner further submits that, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 65 years as on the date of accident.
He was Real Estate Business and self employed and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He was maintaining his family out of said source of income and was a sole bread earner to his family.
Due to the accidental injuries he could not able to do any kind of work compared to his previous strategy.
The disability sustained in the accident has impacted on his earning capacity and as such himself and his family have suffered a lot by mentally, physically and financially.
6. The accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driver of the respondent No.2, who drive his vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3437.

The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the said vehicle thereby the vicarious liability is operated on respondent No.1 on the indemnified contract and as such, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till realization.
8. After registration of the petition, notices were issued against respondents.
notices were issued against respondents.
Inspite of service of the notice, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before this court.
Hence, after due service of notice against the respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 is placed exparte.
In pursuance of service of notice the respondent No.1 has appeared through their counsel and has filed their written statement on behalf of respondent No.1 by denying the entire petition averments.
The respondent No.1 further pleaded that the insurance policy was in force as on the date of the accident and liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further denied the age of the petitioner, avocation, income, injuries sustained, treatment underwent by the petitioner, disability certificate obtained by the petitioner, medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment of the said petitioner.
Further denied the other contents of the petition.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
9. In order to substantiate his claim, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 16 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.23.

In addition to his evidence, the petitioner got examined Medical Records Department at Aster RV Hospital and also got examined doctor, who has issued disability certificate for the injuries sustained by as PW.2 and PW.3 respectively.
Thereby the evidence of petitioner side was completed and case was posted for respondent evidence.
The respondent No.2 has examined the driver of the respondent No.2 vehicle as RW.1 and no documents marked on his behalf.

10. Heard the arguments on both side and perused the materials on record.
11.

Based on the above said pleading, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner prove that, he has sustained grievous in- juries due to the actionable negligent driving of TATA Ace Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3437 by its driver, in RTA took place on 22.01.2022 at about 6.30 p.m., on 100 feet road, near Kalikamba Nandini Booth, Vajarahalli, Bengaluru?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
12. My findings on the above issues are as under.
for the following:-

sentences.text: The petitioner has made stand towards fact and factum of the accident that on 22.01.2022 at about 06.30 p.m., the petitioner was crossing the road on Vajarahalli, 100 feet road, near Kalikamba Nandini booth.
At that time one Tata Ace bearing Reg.No.KA-05- AD-3437 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact of a accident the petitioner fell down and has sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

14. The petitioner has claimed compensation against the respondents urging that the alleged accident took place on the alleged date, time, place and thereby the petitioner was called upon to substantiate the said stand.
15.
By responding to the one way burden the petitioner has come up with oral and documentary evidence.
The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 23 documents in total on his behalf.
Further, PW.1 has got marked 16 documents on his behalf as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.

Further,
petitioner got examined Medical Records as PW.2 got marked 3 documents through the said PW.2 as per Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.19. Further, the petitioner got examined doctor as PW.3, who has issued disability certificate to him and got marked 4 documents through the said PW.3 as per Ex.P20 to Ex.P23.
In his chief-examination, PW.1 has reiterated the petition averments and has specifically stated that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offender vehicle.
16. The respondent No.2 has examined driver of respondent No.2 vehicle as RW.1 by name Venkataramu.
and no documents marked on his behalf.
In his chief- examination the said RW.1 has deposed that he was conversant with the facts of this case.
On 22.01.2022 at about 6.30 p.m., he was driving his TATA Ace bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3437 in a low speed by following traffic rules near 100 feet road of Kanakapura Main Road, near Biyanapalya.
The petitioner under the influence of alcohol as dashed against his vehicle.
Petitioner had fell down and got accident for himself.
The alleged accident was not due to his fault and therefore he is not guilt of the alleged offence.

Hence,
prayed to dismiss the petition.
17. RW.1 was subjected to cross-examination by learned counsel for the petitioner.
During the course of cross-examination RW.1 has admitted that he has not lodged any complaint against the petitioner before the police.
The police have filed charge sheet against him for the alleged accident.
He has not furnished any document to show that he has challenged the charge sheet stating that the accident was not occurred by his fault.
18. Per contra, the evidence of PW.1 clearly reveals that the accident has took place by the fault of the offender vehicle driver i.e., RW.1.
During the course of further cross-examination of PW.1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1, so as to disbelieve his version.
Hence, this court is of the view that the petitioner has proved that due to the rash and negligent driver of the TATA Ace driver the accident has took place on the day of accident.

sentences.text: The accident in question is not in dispute.

Whereas Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint,
Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar along with sketch, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report, Ex.P13 is the charge sheet which clearly shows that, on the alleged date, time and place of the accident has occurred and in the said accident the offender vehicle is involved in the occurrence of the same.
20. The above referred documents clearly indicates that, the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.2 offender vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AD-3437.
It is clear from the records that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and extended with treatment.
There is no any adverse material available to disbelieve the stand taken by the petitioner to the extent of the factum of accident as introduced by him.
Thus, this tribunal has answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
21.
The petitioner has claimed compensation for a sum of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till its realization.
On the basis of the materials on record, it is necessary to examine claim of petitioner in appropriate manner.
In support of the case petitioner has come up with various materials.
As such it is necessary to examined the materials on record in the parameter of pecuniary and non-pecuniary character.

1. Pecuniary loss:- This head of compensation includes compensation towards the loss of earning capacity, medical and future medical expenditure, expenditure incurred towards conveyance allowance, attendant charges, special diet and other miscellaneous expenditure.
As such these aspects are to be examined by examining the available materials on record.

(A) Loss of earning capacity and loss of future income/earnings:-
In order to determine the compensation under this head, it is necessary to consider the age of injured person, occupation, quantum of income, nature of injuries,
percentage of disability and multiplier applicable are to be worked out on the available materials.
(i) The age and applicable multiplier:- The petitioner has contended in his petition that, as on the date of accident he was aged about 65 years.

The material pertaining to Cr.No.16/22 and other medical documents contemplated as on the date of accident,
the petitioner was aged about 65 years.
In addition to that, the petitioner has placed his reliance on the copy of aadhar card.
The said aadhar card reflected the date of birth of petitioner as 17.07.1956.
The accident has occurred on 22.01.2022.

Upon computing the age of the petitioner based on all these materials, it clearly shows that,
the petitioner is aged of 66 years as on the date of occurrence of accident.
As per the documentary evidence available on record, the age of the petitioner is considered as 66 years as on the date of the accident.

Applying the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others Case reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298,

(ii) The occupation of petitioner and quantum of income:- The petitioner has contended that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and was Real estate business and self employed and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He has not produced any documents to prove the said income.
Hence, in the absence of express proof, it is necessary to determine the income of the petitioner based on the principles of notional income.
The Karnataka State Legal Service Authority has fixed a chart for notional income.
By placing reliance on the said income slab.
The income of the petitioner is to be determined.
As per the said chart the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month as operated to the year 2022.
The annual income of the petitioner shall arrive at Rs.1,86,000/- (Rs.15,500 X 12)
(iii) Nature of injury and percentage of disability:-

To prove the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner he has examined one doctor Shailesh., Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bengaluru, is examined as PW.3 and got marked 4 documents as per Ex.P.20 to Ex.P.23.
PW.3/ doctor
has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained mid brain hemorrhage and diffuse axonal injury.
This witness has opined that, petitioner has sustained permanent physical disability to the whole body at 40%.
The injuries are permanent in nature.
Petitioner has contended that, he is a Real estate Business and self employed and assessed disability causes effect on the avocation of petitioner.
Hence, the disability is considered at 40%.
The said extent of disability is considerable to determine the compensation under this head.

To prove the nature of his injuries the petitioner has examined one Jegan, Medical Records Department, Aster RV Hospital, J.P.Nagar, Bengaluru, as PW.2, though him, authorization letter,
police intimation letter and inpatient case file which are marked under Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.19.
These documents shows that petitioner has taken treatment in Aster RV Hospital.
Annual income X Multiplier X permanent physical disability = Loss of earning capacity.
Thereby the petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,72,000/- towards loss of earning capacity and future earnings.
The petitioner being a Real estate business and self- employment and contended that, he used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month.
As the petitioner has not produced any documents to prove his income.
In the absence of proof, the notional income is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Under the circumstances, the per day income of the petitioner would arrive at Rs.517/-.
As per the discharge summaries the petitioner was admitted to hospital as an inpatient for 56 days and after discharge from the hospital there must be necessary to take bed rest for at least 94 days.
So, the petitioner is entitled to compensation towards laid up period with one attendant charge at the same rate which comes to Rs.1,55,100/- (150 days X 517 = Rs.77,550 + 77,550).

6 (B) Medical and future medical expenditure:-

sentences.text: The petitioner contended that, he has incurred Rs.20,00,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance, medical treatment, attendant and nursing care expenses.
The petitioner has placed his reliance on medical bills.
On perusal of the same it is arrived at Rs.7,51,940/- as per medical records.
Further the petitioner has claimed compensation towards future medical expenditure for follow up treatment.
The x-ray shows that the petitioner required further medical expenses of Rs.50,000/-.
By considering the medical and future medical expenditure, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.8,01,940/- (Rs.7,51,940/- + Rs.50,000/-) under this head.
(c) Conveyance allowances, attendant charge and special diet:-
As per the available material it is clear that the petitioner was under treatment for a period of 66 days with extended follow up treatment.
This shows that petitioner has incurred expenditure towards conveyance to meet his treatment.

Further the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries in the accident and has taken assistance of attendant including the assistance of his family members, for which they have suffered loss of income.
This shows that the petitioner has sustained loss towards attendants.
Further the petitioner has sustained fracture injury and attended medication.
This shows that the petitioner has followed the nutrition to meet with her necessary protein and special diet.
By considering all these aspects, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.80,000/- to the petitioner under this head.

22. Non-Pecuniary Loss:- This element of compensation reads as follows;
(a) Pain and sufferings and mental agony:-
According to medical records, the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries at the age of 66 years as on the date of accident.
The said accidental injuries have caused him lot of pain to suffer in his future life span.
By considering the nature of the injuries and percentage of disability caused to the petitioner, the petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

(b) Loss of enjoyment of life and amenities of life:-
The available on records reveals that the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries at the age of 66 years as on the date of accident.
This shows that the injuries caused to petitioner has impacted on the enjoyment of his personal life and amenities of life.
Hence, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.60,000/- under this head.

24. Admittedly, the respondent No.1 and 2 are the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer is bound to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Hence, respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
25.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.15,69,040/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
